exposure: Women who delivered via cesarean section
Delivery method (Cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
Maternal race/ethnicity (Black, Asian, Hispanic vs. non-Hispanic White)
cohort: 688 cases of women with hospitalized VTE within 3 months post-delivery and 10,246 controls of postpartum women without VTE
finding: Maternal race/ethnicity is associated with the risk of postpartum VTE, independently of other risk factors, and should be considered when assessing the use of thromboprophylaxis after delivery.
mod_finding: Black women had a greater risk of postpartum VTE compared with white women among women who delivered via cesarean section, but not among vaginal deliveries.
